Q: turn my html+css+php code into a PDF as an email attachment A:

Installation of a PDF generation library (e.g. TCPDF / mPDF) via Composer should not be difficult. The main advantage is that Composer will detect the suitable library version for you based on the PHP version you installed.

Normally you will not encounter many "errorcodes" when installing the composer itself. For example, if you are using Windows, then you may simply (1) install XAMPP based on the PHP version you prefer (2) Install composer, which will check the PHP version (of the XAMPP) of your system during installation (3) run the necessary composer installation command (For example it will be composer require tecnickcom/tcpdf if you are installing tcpdf) and you will get all the necessary files inside the vendor folder (4) upload the vendor folder (which contains all the sub-directories and files required) to the web server when you need to deploy the TCPDF library.

Q: Alter a SQL Server table column size in production A:

Now, sometime later. There is the dependency proxy:

Q: Serilog.Sinks.Graylog works from a Web API app but does not appear to work from console app A:

I am having the same problem with a .net 10 Console app. After changing the SelfLog to

Serilog.Debugging.SelfLog.Enable(msg => System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine(msg));

I was able to see the following error which was being absorbed.

2026-03-17T14:45:59.3166262Z Oops something going wrong System.InvalidOperationException: IP address could not be resolved.
   at Serilog.Sinks.Graylog.Core.Transport.Udp.UdpTransportClient.EnsureTarget()
   at Serilog.Sinks.Graylog.Core.Transport.Udp.UdpTransportClient.Send(Byte[] payload)
   at Serilog.Sinks.Graylog.GraylogSink.EmitAsync(LogEvent logEvent)
   at Serilog.Sinks.Graylog.GraylogSink.Emit(LogEvent logEvent)

I have tried with both DNS name and IP address. Same error either way

Q: Running 32bit windows application inside docker (or Linux wine) A:

Wrong question

You're repeating the same question, not clarifying anything. Especially why you want to run a Windows app on Linux, when you already have a Linux version. Or what this question has to do with software engineering. Is this a licensing issue?

I already answered anyway.

If the VM runs on Google Cloud, everything already runs on a VM, as fast as the provider allows. Even containers will run on a host VM, never directly on Google servers. If you want faster performance, use a more powerful VM. And run the Linux version of MetaTrader on it.

You can't use containers to speed things up. Containers only isolate processes and services on the same OS. You can't use emulation if you want better performance. Things will run a LOT slower, if at all.
